panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows lung histology demonstrating diffuse interstitial thickening and proliferation, consistent with the histological findings in genetic surfactant dysfunction. B: Panel B displays high-power view showing type II pneumocyte hyperplasia and presence of eosinophilic amorphous material, consistent with genetic surfactant dysfunction pathology. C: Panel C confirms the presence of PAS-positive amorphous material in the alveolar spaces, supporting the diagnosis of genetic surfactant dysfunction based on histological staining.

in_text_mentions: A chest computed tomography (CT) scan with intravenous contrast revealed bilateral diffuse perihilar consolidation and airspace opacities sparing the apices and basal regions (Figure 2), which remained unchanged on follow‐up high‐resolution CT. A sagittal contrast‐enhanced reconstruction further demonstrated the persistent bilateral pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities and diffuse air‐space opacities, supporting the chronic nature of the disease (Figure 3). A rigid bronchoscopy showed a patent airway with no H‐type tracheoesophageal fistula. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy was grossly normal.
